scope: Actual queue application guard, immutable journal borrowing during callbacks/business mutation, privately constructed success confirmation, diagnostic-only entry gate, fresh complete recovery and byte-prefix composition.

properties.queue_application::{arm,apply,confirm}: Arm changes only the actual journal poison flag. apply requires the guard, borrows the journal immutably and describes the exact business state on before-hook, partial-body and after-hook failures. Only successful full business application and both successful hooks create Confirmation. confirm consumes the private non-Clone token and clears only the poison flag, under its stated journal-state binding.
properties.queue_application::{hook_result,applicat: The exact callback history distinguishes before/after and success/failure. Before errors preserve business state, body errors retain their exact partial transaction prefix, and after errors follow complete application. Callback return errors cannot be silently converted to success under this contract.
properties.queue_application::permitted: The actual Coordinator::call gate admits non-diagnostic operations only when the journal is unpoisoned and open. Diagnostic state access retains its original exception.
properties.queue_application::{restore,rebuilt_fold: A poisoned input is rejected. A usable decoded journal is armed before initialization/replay. Return errors keep it quarantined; success alone returns an independently constructed complete business state and clears the flag. No partially applied business state is an input to this rebuild.
properties.journal_equivalence::restored_prefix: The returned fresh business state is the ordered event fold of the actual successful parser Values from the accepted physical byte prefix, excluding its identity header. This does not infer full numeric representation equality from observations.
properties.native integration: CommitIo stores the successful confirmation until execute_commit reaches confirm_apply. ApplyHooks calls the same before_commit_apply/after_commit_apply Fault names. Coordinator::open moves Restored fields into the object only after success; the old in-place apply_transaction body is replaced by the verified application function.

specification_sensitivity.scope: Specification sensitivity, not a production bug: deleting only the hook-result postcondition permits the same ignored-after-error code mutation to verify. With the postcondition retained, application_after_error_ignored is a semantic failure in the full campaign.
specification_sensitivity.reproduce: Copy the exact positive source inputs into an isolated directory, apply both recorded mutations to changed_path, and run the pinned positive Verus command with command_suffix. Require successful verification of apply; the strong-contract algorithm mutant must separately fail semantically.

boundaries: ENV-QUEUE-APPLICATION-HOOKS supplies the lower invocation/result trace, not successful callbacks, termination, durability, business/cache correctness or rollback. No serde primitive or whole straw algorithm is added to the trusted surface.
Native ApplyHooks name/result mapping and CommitIo confirmation-slot/current-context correspondence are reviewed and regression-tested, not separately verified through the complete Coordinator type.

The confirmation proof binds journal State values; it is not physical File identity. Public mutable Rust fields, native File/run/fencing/lock mapping, derived caches, recovered-consumption identities and complete catalog/GC composition remain open.
Normal-return Verus proofs do not model arbitrary Rust unwinding. Existing native before/after apply panic regressions check caught-unwind quarantine and accepted-data GC protection.
No new production defect is claimed. The mutation experiment demonstrates a specification omission, not a valid-API data-loss witness.

The private confirmation is a zero-sized native value held in an Option by CommitIo. Recovery still initializes one business state and borrows decoded history. No new I/O or persistent format change; no measured zero-overhead or throughput claim.
